subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Acme Commerce (post-demo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme-commerce.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@acme-commerce.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:47:00-08:00
Subject: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Acme Commerce (post-demo)

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today, Samir — really appreciate the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we learned (high level):
- Primary use case: reduce per-query inference cost and latency for search/rerank across product pages (peak traffic 6PM PST).
- Current pain: inconsistent latency at scale and manual model swaps; procurement wants predictable pricing and a clear SOC2 profile.
- Timing: procurement + security evaluation in parallel; target procurement decision by end of Q1.

Decisions & asks:
1) Can you share a simple org chart or list of who will be involved on the Acme side (economic buyer, security, legal/procurement, and engineering owners)? If you can attach a one-page org chart that would be ideal.
2) We’ll prepare a short mutual action plan (MAP) and SOC2 summary for your security team — I’ll loop in our security/CS leads.
3) Proposed next meeting: 30 min with VP Product (to align on decision criteria) + 30 min with Head of Procurement (to go over terms). Any availability next week?

I’m CC’ing Lydia here to keep product context and to make scheduling easier. I’ll also pull together the MAP and SOC2 summary and share by EOD tomorrow.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf (stub)

Subject: Re: Stakeholder mapping & next steps — Acme Commerce (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa — great demo. Quick answers inline and a couple of asks: 

Thanks for the recap. We can share an org chart; attaching a working file — will confirm the names. High level stakeholders:
- Economic buyer: Tom Alvarez (VP, Revenue Ops) — he owns budget approvals for infrastructure.
- Security: Lydia is the main technical contact and will route any SOC/compliance work to our InfoSec team.
- Procurement/legal: Our procurement lead will be involved once we have initial pricing/terms — I can intro once you have the MAP.

Asks from our side:
- Can you include a sample SLA target and typical pricing cadence in the MAP (monthly committed vs. burst usage model)?
- Do you have a one-page summary of telemetry/logging and data retention we can share with procurement?

I’m attaching the org chart draft (Acme_OrgChart_v2.pdf) — it still needs a couple of names filled in. I’ll follow up with Tom and procurement once we have a MAP and the SOC2 summary.

— Samir

Thanks for the loop, Marissa. Quick updates from security/compliance side: 

- I’ve attached the SOC2 summary and the telemetry one-pager for procurement (Redwood_SOC2_Summary.pdf). These are customer-friendly docs — if Acme’s InfoSec needs the full audit, we’ll coordinate an NDA and provide the auditor contact.
- On logging/telemetry: we retain inference logs for 90 days by default; we can offer extended retention as an add-on. The one-pager includes fields we typically expose (request_id, model_version, latency, token_counts).
- Rafael — can you prepare a short bullet list for procurement on standard contract terms we surface (data ownership, EULA, support/response windows)?

I’ll be available for a 30-min sync with Acme InfoSec next week if Samir makes the intro.

— Monica
